已查到可引用的部分資料：

### Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI, the evidence must directly cover the same AI test use case, same measurement method, same R&S configuration/options, and verified competitor capabilities; the current passages support an R&S CMX500 generative AI user-experience testbed but do not provide an AI-specific, evidence-backed competitor comparison [37][82].  
### Evidence required
| Required evidence | Why it is required | Current support / gap |
|---|---|---|
| A defined AI test use case and architecture, such as generative AI application user-experience testing with LLM on server/cloud, CMX500 radio connection to a smart terminal, configurable network parameters, fading, latency, jitter, and RF impairments | Without a shared AI test scenario, any comparison would mix unlike use cases | The R&S AI use case is described for CMX500, but only for the R&S/China Mobile demo context [37]. |
| A measurement methodology for AI KPIs such as TTFT and TPS, including prompt set, LLM model, server/cloud configuration, terminal model, radio scenarios, statistical treatment, and reproducibility data | Without methodology, KPI comparisons would be unsupported | The source lists TTFT and TPS as KPIs, but explicitly lacks measurement methodology, prompt set, LLM model, server/cloud configuration, terminal model, scenario table, statistical treatment, and reproducibility data [37][82]. |
| Actual measured data, benchmark charts, or a public report for the AI testbed | Without results, claims about better AI user experience or benchmark leadership are unsupported | The source explicitly says it does not provide measured data, benchmark charts, or a public report for the MWC Shanghai 2026 demo [82]. |
| Formal R&S configuration evidence: hardware configuration, software version, option/order numbers, and supported measurement scope for the AI setup | Without configuration evidence, the comparison cannot be tied to an orderable or reproducible solution | The AI PR source does not provide solution order number, software version, or CMX500 hardware configuration [82]. |
| Binding R&S specifications and feature documents for Signaling capabilities, rather than sales/training claims | Product capability claims need formal specifications or feature documents, not positioning slides | The CMX500 page separates binding specifications from feature/function overview, and notes that data without tolerance limits is not binding [57]. |
| Formal evidence for Non-signaling capabilities, including license boundaries and release status | Non-signaling claims need to distinguish base GPRF generation from licensed technology-specific waveform/ARB functions | GPRF Generator is described as a CMX500 non-signaling use case, but “No License required” must be separated from technology-specific ARB / WinIQSim2 licensing, and planned features require release-note verification [28][29]. |
| Official competitor datasheets, release notes, support terms, and third-party evidence for competitor capabilities | Internal battle cards alone are not enough to state competitor weaknesses or advantages | The Anritsu comparison page says customer documents should additionally check Anritsu official material and third-party evidence [9]. |
| Official competitor evidence for Amarisoft claims, not only R&S internal battle-card positioning | Internal battle-card claims about Amarisoft are single-source sales positioning | The Amarisoft comparison page says claims currently come only from an R&S internal battle card and should be checked against Amarisoft official material and third-party evidence [12]. |
| Side-by-side evidence for the same AI scenario, metrics, network conditions, DUT/client, and pass/fail or benchmark criteria | A valid comparison must connect both sides to the same use case and conditions | The available AI source describes only the R&S/China Mobile CMX500 testbed, while the competitor pages are sales positioning and not AI-specific benchmark evidence [37][7][10]. |
| Clear exclusion of sales-language claims such as “only platform,” “industry-leading,” “safe and future-proof,” or “lower TCO” unless independently verified | These phrases are not verifiable technical specifications | The Anritsu page says such phrases are sales language, and the Amarisoft page says “Only R&S” and “safe and future-proof choice” are sales language rather than verifiable technical specifications [9][12]. |
### What cannot be claimed from the current passages
We cannot claim our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester is better than a competitor for AI, because the AI evidence describes an R&S CMX500 generative AI testbed but does not include competitor data, measurement methodology, reproducibility data, or benchmark results [37][82].  
We cannot use the Anritsu or Amarisoft battle cards alone as proof of competitor limitations in an AI comparison, because those pages identify the battle cards as sales positioning rather than binding technical specifications and require official competitor or third-party validation for customer-facing use [7][9][10][12].  
We cannot turn CMX500 AI PR wording into a formal product configuration or quotation basis, because the AI source lacks hardware configuration, software version, order number, and measurement methodology [82].

R&S CMX500 vs Anritsu › Sales landmines
[[2026_02_CMX500_Anritsu_Sales_Battle_Card]] 建議用以下問題區分需求：

1. 是否需要 FR1 bandwidth beyond 400 MHz，例如 600–800 MHz per carrier for 5G-Advanced Rel-18 / Rel-19 testing？
2. 是否需要 FR1、FR2、FR3、WLAN 與 LTE 在 single instrument 中且不用 hardware swaps？
3. 是否需要 native fading with high-throughput IP testing？
4. 是否偏好 one unified software platform，而不是 four separate tools？
5. 是否需要 advanced CA 或 mobility without adding extra boxes？
6. 是否需要 FR3 testing beyond 16 GHz，以支援 emerging 6G FR3 evaluations？

R&S CMX500 vs Anritsu › R&S offensive plays

- Multi-SIM 部分描述 DSDS / DSDA：1 DUT、2 SIM slots、2 parallel connections、1 CMX；DSDS 通常 one TX / 2 RX、2 SIMs standby、一次一個 active connection；DSDA 為 two TRX、2 SIMs active connection at a time；option 線索為 [[R&S CMX-KS600B]] NR Signaling SA/NSA 與 [[R&S CMX-KS613B]] Multi-SIM Enabler。
- Callbox example use cases 包含 R&D verification of new bands、sensitivity testing、RedCap、de-sense testing、3GPP pre-conformance、SRS measurements、UL MIMO and UL CA RF measurements、UL TX Switching、Multi-SIM、high e2e TP testing 與 non-signaling verification。

- SRS / UL MIMO / UL TX Switching 部分稱 CMX supports all SRS modes / configurations，SRS measurements 可量測 TX power、EVM 等，[[R&S CMX-KS610B]] 用於 SRS carrier switching；UL MIMO RF measurements 提到 [[R&S CMX-KM604]] NR FR1 measurements MIMO、PC 1.5、29 dBm theoretical sum power for 2 TX antennas、UL FPTX、TX diversity、DFTS-OFDM。
- NTN 部分稱 comprehensive support for NR-NTN，multi-orbit：LEO、MEO、GEO、GSO，complete channel emulation in one box，live graphics for NTN orbits and parameters，NB-NTN coming end of `25，option 線索為 [[R&S CMX-KS627B]] NR Signaling Extension Rel-17。

### Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI, the evidence must directly cover the same AI test use case, same measurement method, same R&S configuration/options, and verified competitor capabilities; the current passages support an R&S CMX500 generative AI user-experience testbed but do not provide an AI-specific, evidence-backed competitor comparison [37][82].  
### Evidence required
| Required evidence | Why it is required | Current support / gap |
|---|---|---|
| A defined AI test use case and architecture, such as generative AI application user-experience testing with LLM on server/cloud, CMX500 radio connection to a smart terminal, configurable network parameters, fading, latency, jitter, and RF impairments | Without a shared AI test scenario, any comparison would mix unlike use cases | The R&S AI use case is described for CMX500, but only for the R&S/China Mobile demo context [37]. |
| A measurement methodology for AI KPIs such as TTFT and TPS, including prompt set, LLM model, server/cloud configuration, terminal model, radio scenarios, statistical treatment, and reproducibility data | Without methodology, KPI comparisons would be unsupported | The source lists TTFT and TPS as KPIs, but explicitly lacks measurement methodology, prompt set, LLM model, server/cloud configuration, terminal model, scenario table, statistical treatment, and reproducibility data [37][82]. |
| Actual measured data, benchmark charts, or a public report for the AI testbed | Without results, claims about better AI user experience or benchmark leadership are unsupported | The source explicitly says it does not provide measured data, benchmark charts, or a public report for the MWC Shanghai 2026 demo [82]. |
| Formal R&S configuration evidence: hardware configuration, software version, option/order numbers, and supported measurement scope for the AI setup | Without configuration evidence, the comparison cannot be tied to an orderable or reproducible solution | The AI PR source does not provide solution order number, software version, or CMX500 hardware configuration [82]. |
| Binding R&S specifications and feature documents for Signaling capabilities, rather than sales/training claims | Product capability claims need formal specifications or feature documents, not positioning slides | The CMX500 page separates binding specifications from feature/function overview, and notes that data without tolerance limits is not binding [57]. |
| Formal evidence for Non-signaling capabilities, including license boundaries and release status | Non-signaling claims need to distinguish base GPRF generation from licensed technology-specific waveform/ARB functions | GPRF Generator is described as a CMX500 non-signaling use case, but “No License required” must be separated from technology-specific ARB / WinIQSim2 licensing, and planned features require release-note verification [28][29]. |
| Official competitor datasheets, release notes, support terms, and third-party evidence for competitor capabilities | Internal battle cards alone are not enough to state competitor weaknesses or advantages | The Anritsu comparison page says customer documents should additionally check Anritsu official material and third-party evidence [9]. |
| Official competitor evidence for Amarisoft claims, not only R&S internal battle-card positioning | Internal battle-card claims about Amarisoft are single-source sales positioning | The Amarisoft comparison page says claims currently come only from an R&S internal battle card and should be checked against Amarisoft official material and third-party evidence [12]. |
| Side-by-side evidence for the same AI scenario, metrics, network conditions, DUT/client, and pass/fail or benchmark criteria | A valid comparison must connect both sides to the same use case and conditions | The available AI source describes only the R&S/China Mobile CMX500 testbed, while the competitor pages are sales positioning and not AI-specific benchmark evidence [37][7][10]. |
| Clear exclusion of sales-language claims such as “only platform,” “industry-leading,” “safe and future-proof,” or “lower TCO” unless independently verified | These phrases are not verifiable technical specifications | The Anritsu page says such phrases are sales language, and the Amarisoft page says “Only R&S” and “safe and future-proof choice” are sales language rather than verifiable technical specifications [9][12]. |
### What cannot be claimed from the current passages
We cannot claim our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester is better than a competitor for AI, because the AI evidence describes an R&S CMX500 generative AI testbed but does not include competitor data, measurement methodology, reproducibility data, or benchmark results [37][82].  
We cannot use the Anritsu or Amarisoft battle cards alone as proof of competitor limitations in an AI comparison, because those pages identify the battle cards as sales positioning rather than binding technical specifications and require official competitor or third-party validation for customer-facing use [7][9][10][12].  
We cannot turn CMX500 AI PR wording into a formal product configuration or quotation basis, because the AI source lacks hardware configuration, software version, order number, and measurement methodology [82].
